notes: Overlay text keeps its size: drag a corner of its frame to scale it, or give it a fixed box where long text scrolls.
A fixed box can shrink long text or cut it off instead, and you pick the scroll speed, a pause and soft edges under Look.
Each row has one ··· menu with Settings, Move up, Move down and Delete; dragging rows works again.
Loads a little lighter: the app keeps only the Latin letters of its fonts.
Add shows the same icons as the list, so you see what each one becomes.
A new clock or counter starts with Words and Number both at M.
Format is a field with a list of formats to pick from, in the same order every time; you can still type your own.
Delete is a button on each row, shown when you point at it. It deletes at once, and Undo brings it back.
Words and Number have the same five sizes, XS to XL, the same as the text sizes in Tavora. Saved sizes move to the nearest one.
Settings opened from the Overlay page show their layout right away instead of an empty window.
Dialogs you open with the keyboard appear instantly.
Toasts wait while the panel is hidden or the game is in front, and slide in and out from their edge.
Settings ask Tavora for the usual dialog size through the shared settings parts; nothing looks different.
Settings use Tavora's settings layout: what the panel shows, what the overlay shows and the stream link, each in its own place.
Write what the overlay says yourself, with {time} or {count}, and see it change as you type.
The words and the number of the overlay get their own colour and size.
In game and On stream say where it shows; Arrange in Overlays opens Tavora's Overlay page.
There is no Done button any more: changes save as you make them, and Delete is the last row of the first page.
Screen readers read each message once.
Settings are tidier: pages on the left and one footer with Delete and Done.
The settings window is named after the clock or counter.
Over game is gone from the settings. Add clocks and counters to your game on the Overlay page.
Drag a row to put it in a new place, or press Alt and the up or down arrow on it.
Main buttons and badges can follow a theme's deeper button colour.
Small update to the shared look; nothing changes for you here.
Lists, dialogs and settings pages move smoothly.
Switches and tabs slide to what you pick.
A counter counts up or down to its new number.
Buttons have a little depth and feel pressed when you click them.
Checkboxes, toggles and options animate when you pick them, and folding sections open smoothly.
Settings in a dialog have an icon and a Close button in the corner.
Menus and tooltips open out of the spot they belong to, and buttons dip a little when you press them.
Add each clock, counter or linked group to your game from the Overlay page, one by one, and place them where you like. A new frame fits its content.
Press the gear on a frame to change that clock, counter or group right over the Overlay page.
In the overlay, the name and the value now share one font and sit on one line.
In a linked group's line, counters now have short names without spaces: {counter2}, {bossKills}, {sitUps}. Tap a counter below the field to add it. Lines you wrote with full names keep working.
Show Clock & Counter over your game from the panel's menu. Your clocks and counters stay in view, and you count or start and stop them while you hold the game layer key.
Add works over your game too, and a button that can't work there now tells you what to do.
A clock or counter's settings now open as a big dialog over the whole workspace, not inside the small panel.
Every clock and counter is a single row now, so more of them fit in a panel. Settings open in a dialog in the middle, behind the gear.
Counters you linked stand together in a frame, and say what they add to and where they count from.
Show a whole group of linked counters in one overlay, with a line you write yourself like {Deaths} Death – {Sit-ups} Situps.
Text fields and dropdowns look calmer in Dark mode.
Countdowns, stopwatches and counters for each game.
Show any of them in OBS, and control them with hotkeys.
